claims.claim_text: Second-hand test equipment markets are badly mispriced at the edges: a 300 MHz four-channel Tektronix DPO4034 with probes plus a Fluke 87 multimeter, a current-model combination listing near ten thousand dollars, sold for five hundred dollars on a local classifieds site.
claims.quote_verbatim: a 300 megahertz Tektronix DPO 4034 four-channel scope with probes and a Fluke 87 for 500 bucks
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Transistor Types and Where To Get Electronic Gear

claims.claim_text: Capability and cash are interchangeable in the used-instrument market: a 300 MHz four-channel scope realising six to seven thousand dollars on resale could be replaced by a second-hand 500 MHz Agilent of comparable sample rate for around four thousand, leaving three to four thousand dollars in hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: a 500 megahertz Agilent scope with similar sort of sample rate and performance secondhand on eBay for four grand
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Transistor Types and Where To Get Electronic Gear

claims.claim_text: A purchasing rule for test equipment is to buy the cheapest option until it demonstrably will not do the job, because most work uses only base functionality and the real limitation announces itself clearly when it arrives, which also identifies exactly which specification the replacement must improve.
claims.quote_verbatim: go as cheap as you can until you can't use it anymore
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Transistor Types and Where To Get Electronic Gear

claims.claim_text: The BNC shells on a mains-powered bench oscilloscope are bonded to mains earth, so clipping the ground lead to any node that is not at earth potential shorts that node to earth through the instrument. This is the standard mechanism by which scopes and circuits are destroyed during work on mains-referenced equipment, and it is why battery-powered floating scopes are used for service work.
claims.quote_verbatim: those B and C connectors are mains-earth reference
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Military Electronics and The Free Eagle (Freagle) Campaign

claims.claim_text: Oscilloscope probes are microphonic: the piezoelectric effect is present in essentially every probe, so mechanical stimulation of the probe body produces a signal at the scope input, with an orientation dependence.
claims.quote_verbatim: So, yes, the piezoelectric effect in probes.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Keyzer - Comical Keyzer Comes a-Callin'

claims.claim_text: Early tablet-tethered mixed-signal instruments paired a single analogue channel of roughly 12 megasamples per second with four digital inputs, with the phone or tablet supplying the display and user interface.
claims.quote_verbatim: one analog input that does something like 12 mega samples per second. And then there's four digital inputs
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Keyzer - Exhilarating ESC Escapades

claims.claim_text: The entry-level oscilloscope bandwidth stayed at 25 MHz, rising to 50 MHz, for many years, because a manufacturer that unilaterally raises the low-end specification must build enough volume to supply the whole segment rather than just its own customers.
claims.quote_verbatim: the entry level oscilloscope up until very recently has still been you know that 25 megahertz maybe it upped it to 50
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Rigol collapsed the price of its 100 MHz model to that of its 50 MHz model, which had been 399 dollars, making the lower-bandwidth unit obsolete overnight and giving owners of the 50 MHz version a straight resell-and-rebuy path in place of the firmware bandwidth hack.
claims.quote_verbatim: rigol have now slashed the price of their 100 megahertz model to be the same as their 50 megahertz model
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Probes, not the mainframe, set the practical bandwidth of a high-bandwidth scope: a 1 GHz instrument cannot reach its specification through the supplied 10:1 passive probe, and the active probe that can costs on the order of the scope itself, so a good FET probe can exceed the price of the instrument it plugs into.
claims.quote_verbatim: a good FET probe can be more expensive than your scope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The Rigol 2000 series arrived as a sub-1000-dollar bench scope with a 500 microvolt per division vertical front end and an 8-inch WVGA display, a vertical sensitivity that had been absent from that price class for many years.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's going to be under $1,000, and that's a hell of a lot of hardware for under $1,000
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Daniher - Nascent Nonolith Numquid

claims.claim_text: 500 microvolts per division is close to the practical floor for vertical sensitivity on a general-purpose bench scope, because the inherent noise of the front end at high bandwidth into a 1 megohm input impedance sets the limit.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't go much lower than that because just the inherent noise floor of the front end
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Daniher - Nascent Nonolith Numquid

claims.claim_text: PC and USB oscilloscopes exist as a separate class because omitting knobs, screen and enclosure removes substantial cost, and because a host-connected instrument can stream continuously to disk for data logging and offer channel counts a bench instrument does not, at the price of much lower sample rates.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can do absolute, like, continuous sampling. You can do data logging and stuff like that, which you can't traditionally do with a bench scope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Ian Daniher - Nascent Nonolith Numquid

claims.claim_text: Extending real-time oscilloscope bandwidth past 100 GHz depends on III-V semiconductor processes rather than silicon: indium phosphide heterojunction bipolar and high-electron-mobility transistor technology, whose wafers and chips are expensive, which is why that capability sits with vertically integrated owners of the process.
claims.quote_verbatim: extending our current oscilloscope path to 100 gigahertz and beyond
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A high-end oscilloscope is a compliance instrument rather than a waveform viewer: it is bought to run automated analysis of high-speed serial signals against a standard such as SATA, including jitter decomposition over billions of measurements to produce an error-rate figure, with the analysis software typically sold as a costly extra rather than built in.
claims.quote_verbatim: this oscilloscope's not designed just to get a waveform on the screen. It's designed to do automated analysis of serial
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Ceramic capacitors & High end scopes - Kempt Kickstarter Kakorrhaphiophobia

claims.claim_text: General-purpose digital oscilloscopes almost universally use 8-bit converters. High-resolution modes recover effective resolution by oversampling and averaging intermediate samples, yielding an effective 10 to 12 bits from an 8-bit converter at reduced bandwidth.
claims.quote_verbatim: most scopes are 8-bit these days
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Tektronix, ChipReport.tv, & the Signal Path - Temperative Tegmen Temperature

claims.claim_text: The Analog Discovery, a roughly 200-dollar USB instrument, pairs a 125 megasample 14-bit converter with a 1 megohm input rated to 20 volts and 250 microvolts per division, though the front-end gain applied to reach that sensitivity costs some of the converter's bits.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's a mega-ohm input. I mean, 20-volt max. It goes down to 250 microvolts per division.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Tektronix, ChipReport.tv, & the Signal Path - Temperative Tegmen Temperature

claims.claim_text: The micro-channel plate CRT, marketed by Tektronix as bright-eye and fitted to a small number of models including the 2467, placed an electron multiplier at the face of the tube that amplified the beam electrons roughly ten thousand times before they struck the phosphor.
claims.quote_verbatim: an electron multiplier right at the face of the CRT so that when the beam was swept across, the electrons that hit this electron multiplier would get magnified 10,000 times
claims.speaker: Alan Wolke

claims.claim_text: The oscilloscope's role changed over two decades from a visualisation and timing-measurement tool to an analysis platform expected to perform compliance measurement against standards, jitter decomposition, and frequency- and modulation-domain analysis in one instrument.
claims.quote_verbatim: people are doing compliance measurements to standards, you know, jitter decomposition, frequency domain, modulation domain analysis
claims.speaker: Alan Wolke

claims.claim_text: Analogue oscilloscopes fall into two classes, recurrent-sweep and triggered-sweep; recurrent-sweep instruments free-run and are far less useful, so a triggered-sweep model is the minimum worth acquiring even when older analogue scopes can be had for the cost of shipping.
claims.quote_verbatim: before triggered scopes, there were the recurrent sweep scopes, which are far less useful
claims.speaker: Alan Wolke

claims.claim_text: A near-free older analogue scope is a rational first instrument: it teaches the fundamentals of what the display is showing, after which a buyer can name the specific features the next instrument must have instead of guessing from specifications.
claims.quote_verbatim: learn about what it does for you and how to use it, how to get the most out of it, and then go decide, okay, I know I need this feature
claims.speaker: Alan Wolke

claims.claim_text: A circuit oscillating above the oscilloscope's bandwidth produces no trace but wrong voltage readings and nonsensical waveforms. Damping the suspect nodes by touch, then soldering in a few picofarads of capacitance between them, both confirms and cures it.
claims.quote_verbatim: I figured that the circuit was probably oscillating at several hundred megahertz, beyond what the scope can show you
claims.speaker: Alan Wolke

claims.claim_text: Instrument documentation specifies capability and is silent on limits, so the measurement error mode that matters is the one outside the tool's stated envelope; the same asymmetry applies to circuit simulators as to scopes.
claims.quote_verbatim: the manuals and everything will tell you everything that the thing can do. But they don't tell you what it can't do
claims.speaker: Alan Wolke

claims.claim_text: Oscilloscope vendors sell sample memory, serial decode and bandwidth as separately licensed options on hardware that already contains the capability, bandwidth in particular being limited in software below what the front end can do.
claims.quote_verbatim: They'll charge more for, you know, sample memory. They'll charge more for serial decode. They'll charge more for bandwidth.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The stated economic case for software-locked instrument options is that leading-edge development is funded by margin on high-end features; selling a fully unlocked 1 GHz decoding scope at four hundred dollars would not sustain the engineering that produced it.
claims.quote_verbatim: if companies can afford to keep people on staff and do leading edge R&D, you have to make money on this higher end margin products
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Linear Technology application note 47 contains a full tutorial on oscilloscopes, probes, connections and grounding, and is the standard reference to hand a student who cannot get a clean trace, since most such failures are instrumentation and grounding problems rather than circuit problems.
claims.quote_verbatim: the app note 47 has, has a whole tutorial on oscilloscopes and probes and connections and grounding
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: The Tektronix 511 was the company's first oscilloscope. The later 556 was a dual-beam plug-in instrument whose two beams and two plug-in slots gave it unusual measurement flexibility.
claims.quote_verbatim: a five 11, which is the first, uh, the first oscilloscope that Tektronix made
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: Tektronix's late-1970s purely analogue 1 GHz oscilloscope was developed to order for the United States Atomic Energy Commission's nuclear weapons testing, on terms of roughly 30,000 dollars each, a committed order of a thousand units, and the right to sell the instrument commercially afterwards.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're going to cost $30,000 and that's, you know, $30,000 in the 1970s to buy you a house
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: High-bandwidth oscilloscopes are export-controlled in the same way as sensitive current-measurement instruments, a restriction rooted in the era when the reason to want a very fast scope was nuclear or weapons instrumentation rather than communications.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're still all export restricted
claims.speaker: Kent Lundberg
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: Acquisition memory moved from 2K samples being a respectable depth, and 8K commanding an extreme price, to a megapoint being available in a 300-dollar instrument.
claims.quote_verbatim: 2k was a decent size sample memory on a scope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Dr. Kent Lundberg - Luculent Linear Legacy

claims.claim_text: Remote or tablet control adds little to an oscilloscope because it is a hands-on instrument: the operator is holding probes on the circuit and is therefore always within arm's reach of the front panel.
claims.quote_verbatim: A scope is a hands-on instrument where you're always probing shit and doing stuff.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Processors, CEOs & Soldering irons - Plentiful Perfunctory Programs

claims.claim_text: Test equipment follows the same deflation as the rest of the industry, with new features and half the previous price appearing annually. Digital oscilloscopes went from nothing under a thousand dollars to capable instruments at 250 to 300 dollars within about five years.
claims.quote_verbatim: five years ago, it was unheard of to buy a digital scope under a thousand bucks
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: FPGA, Xess, 32 Bit - Quirky Qualitative Questions

claims.claim_text: Instrument acquisition inside large organisations is governed by which budget the money comes from, not total cost: rental at two hundred thousand dollars a year can be approved where a fifty-thousand-dollar capital purchase cannot.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't afford that $50,000 scope, but you can afford $200,000 to rent it for a year
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Hardware, Surveys and Giveaways - Radular Rental Ranting

claims.claim_text: Some instrument vendors state that different bandwidth models are physically different hardware when the boards are in fact identical and the difference is a licence setting, which is the factual basis for the argument that unlocking a purchased instrument costs the vendor no unit sale.
claims.quote_verbatim: They will lie that, oh, no, trust me, when we sell you the 100 megahertz version or we sell you the 1 gigahertz version, it's physically different when it's actually not
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Hardware, Surveys and Giveaways - Radular Rental Ranting

claims.claim_text: Field-upgradeable bandwidth and features suit corporate procurement, where spending above a capital-expenditure threshold requires senior approval: a lower-specification instrument clears the threshold now and incremental licence upgrades can be bought a year at a time.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can buy the low, quote-unquote, low-end one, right? That's one purchase. And then next year, oh, well, I need more bandwidth or I need this feature.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: PCB Mills, SDR and Oscilloscopes - Flaunting Furbelow Fanciness

claims.claim_text: An oscilloscope has a single trigger point that all channels share, so on a two- or four-channel instrument only signals synchronous with the trigger source stand still. Two inputs differing by one hertz give one stable trace and one that travels across the screen at a one hertz rate, making the second unusable for catching events.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it's one hertz out in frequency, you'll see it travel at one hertz rate across your screen
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: PCB Mills, SDR and Oscilloscopes - Flaunting Furbelow Fanciness

claims.claim_text: The incumbent high-end instrument makers retreated from the low end rather than abandoning basic research: they cannot compete on price with the newer entrants, and the margin, which funds work such as 80 GHz front ends, is at the top of the range.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're going to stop trying to target the low-end. Because they can't compete at the low-end
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Agilent's New Name, Molex's New Owner and PCB artwork - Nonsensical Naming Neolatry

claims.claim_text: A procedure for an unfamiliar signal on an unfamiliar oscilloscope is to set the fastest time base, apply the signal, and slow the time base until something appears, which guarantees the display is never undersampled. Modern instruments with a built-in frequency counter warn of undersampling directly.
claims.quote_verbatim: I put that thing in its fastest time base setting, apply my unknown signal, and then I start dialing it downwards until I see something
claims.speaker: Vincent Himpe
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Vincent Himpe - Escaped Electron Elocution

claims.claim_text: For teaching laboratories the selection criteria for an oscilloscope are warranty and replacement support, the supplied teaching material, and whether the same model will still be purchasable in ten years, since lab notes written for one model must remain valid for its replacements.
claims.quote_verbatim: Will the same scope be available in 10 years' time?
claims.episode_title: What defines an engineer? - Job Judging Jeremiad

claims.claim_text: In an equivalent-time sampling oscilloscope the bandwidth is set entirely by the front-end sample-and-hold, which captures the signal in a window of order ten picoseconds and holds it. The conversion afterwards can be arbitrarily slow, so a ten-cent microcontroller ADC is sufficient behind a 10 GHz front end.
claims.quote_verbatim: for a sampling scope, the bandwidth is all about the sample and hold
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A cheap sampling-scope front end typically has no attenuator and only a 50 ohm SMA input, so probing a high-impedance source requires an active probe costing many times the instrument, and without one the fast edge the instrument exists to capture is rounded off.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's 50 ohm input, you know, SMA connectors, 50 ohm only
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A mixed-domain oscilloscope is defined by synchronous capture across the time and frequency domains. A later cost-reduced model in the same family kept the name but removed that capability, so its spectrum and waveform captures cannot be tied together in time.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't actually tie the two domains together and do synchronous sampling between them
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Someone is watching...we think - Horme Hostility Hypochondriac

claims.claim_text: Test-equipment vendors win educational sales by supplying the courseware: shipping course books that explain how the instrument works removes the lecturer's preparation effort, and instructors buy on the strength of the pre-written material.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's why Agilent sell their oscilloscopes to the education market, right? Because they have, you know, these course books that go with it
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Marcus Schappi - Kit Ketch Kenophobia

claims.claim_text: The two architectures available to a USB instrument are continuous streaming at whatever rate the bus sustains, or a much higher sample rate with local triggering and capture memory that is then read out slowly over the bus; the choice determines whether the device is a data logger or an oscilloscope.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can do something with a much higher sample rate and do triggering and storage and stuff and then, you know, slowly stream the samples over USB
claims.speaker: Michael Ossmann
claims.episode_title: Mike Ossmann Returns! - Planetic Portalab Packaging

claims.claim_text: A significant class of instruments marketed as multimeters or oscilloscopes are data loggers built around a 16-bit converter, specified by accuracy rather than by digits or bandwidth, and should be assessed on the logging specification rather than the label.
claims.quote_verbatim: they've just got a 16-bit ADC in there, and it's just a data logger
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: The 2014 Maker Faire Show - Traveling Technology Trangam

claims.claim_text: Coaxial cable generates charge when flexed, so moving an oscilloscope probe puts a visible blip on the screen. The same triboelectric noise corrupts measurements from charge-output sensors such as accelerometers, where the cable's own charge adds to the sensor's.
claims.quote_verbatim: anytime you move a, uh, uh, oscilloscope probe, right, you're going to see some kind of blip on the screen
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: Wrong Hardware, Wrong Software - Fugacious Fan Funding

claims.claim_text: A dual-processor bus fault was found on the scope as a faint spike on one address line present only when the second processor drove the bus: the inactive processor's connection formed an unterminated stub on the PCB trace. Reading a trace like this requires knowing which of the artefacts on screen are normal.
claims.quote_verbatim: I saw this little ghost of a chip, a little ghost of a spike on A10 when the Z80 was trying to do it
claims.speaker: Bil Herd
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Bil Herd - Zany Z80 Zygology

claims.claim_text: Hybrid analogue and digital storage oscilloscopes were built with a genuine analogue front end and a button that switched the same signal path into a basic megasample digital storage mode, giving both display technologies in one instrument.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's actually got like a analog front end and you can use it in full analog mode or you push a button and it becomes kind of a basic like mega sample digital storage scope
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: MightyHohm For The Holidays - Kaiser Keyzer's Kits

claims.claim_text: Intermittent or dead front-panel controls on an older scope are commonly failed rotary encoders, often from stored moisture ingress. The encoders are frequently generic catalogue parts available from a distributor, and manufacturers have supplied full service manuals on request, making the repair routine.
claims.quote_verbatim: it used a rotary encoder that I could buy on digikey
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell
claims.episode_title: MightyHohm For The Holidays - Kaiser Keyzer's Kits

claims.claim_text: The top of the oscilloscope market reaches a million dollars per instrument, at which point demonstration units are not shipped to prospective customers.
claims.quote_verbatim: this like is a $1 million oscilloscope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Questioning Everyday Prototyping - Verrucose Vehicle Vitilitigation

claims.claim_text: The systems needed to test, calibrate and qualify a gigahertz-class oscilloscope are themselves major instruments, and the requirement scales sharply with the bandwidth being verified.
claims.quote_verbatim: just, just the test systems to actually test and calibrate and qualify a one gig scope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Questioning Everyday Prototyping - Verrucose Vehicle Vitilitigation

claims.claim_text: High-value instrument manufacture does not follow the usual offshoring logic: at fifty to a hundred thousand dollars per unit the labour content is negligible against calibration, qualification and volume, so production stays where the engineering is.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're selling a $50,000, $100,000 scope, you know, there's no advantage to going to China
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Questioning Everyday Prototyping - Verrucose Vehicle Vitilitigation

claims.claim_text: The bandwidth needed to reproduce a given edge is approximately 0.35 over the 10-90 percent rise time. The harmonics of a fast edge fall off but remain significant, so reproducing the edge in the time domain requires retaining frequency content up to that bandwidth.
claims.quote_verbatim: that bandwidth is, turns out, when you do the analysis, is about 0.35 over the rise time
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: The 0.35 over rise time rule assumes a brick-wall response with zero amplitude above the bandwidth; a real front end rolls off gradually, so the rule is an approximation whose error depends on the instrument's actual response shape.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's based on if I have a cliff filter
claims.speaker: Eric Bogatin
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Eric Bogatin - Tilded Thumb Tenets

claims.claim_text: Working on deliberately floating electronics is straightforward until it must be measured, because almost every bench oscilloscope and bench multimeter is earth-referenced; handheld instruments are the usual way out.
claims.quote_verbatim: the tough part is measuring, because almost every scope and every bench DMM
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: SPI and most digital outputs are totem-pole, with transistors driving both directions, while I2C is open-collector and relies on a pull-up resistor for the rising edge. Zooming in on the edge with a scope shows the asymmetry directly: a near-instant fall and an RC-shaped rise.
claims.quote_verbatim: I squared C is an open collector output, essentially. And to pull the line high, you're relying on that pull-up resistor.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The debugging order for a non-working I2C bus is physical layer first: scope the lines to confirm the pull-ups and clean edges, then check chip addressing and enables, and only then question the protocol implementation or the provenance of the library.
claims.quote_verbatim: The first thing I'm going to do is actually get the scope out and just probe it to make sure that there's nothing funny with the pull-up
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The quantisation steps at a DAC output are directly visible by probing the output of an arbitrary waveform generator, zooming in and raising the scope's vertical gain, which is why a reconstruction filter is fitted.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you zoom right in and actually turn the amp and then turn the gain of your scope up, then you can actually see the little steps
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: For a shared or teaching laboratory, ten 100 MHz oscilloscopes are a better use of the same budget than one 1 GHz instrument at around fifteen thousand dollars, because gigahertz bandwidth serves only a handful of specialists working at the edge of high-speed design.
claims.quote_verbatim: You don't put a one gig scope in there. You put in 10, 100 megahertz scopes
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The reason to own an oscilloscope is that it is the only direct view of what a circuit is doing; the corollary is that the user must also understand how that view distorts what it shows.
claims.quote_verbatim: the oscilloscope is your window into what's going on
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Documentation Is A Waste Of Time

claims.claim_text: The OpenScope, built on a Microchip PIC32MZ, combined two roughly six-megasample scope channels at up to 3 MHz analogue bandwidth and plus or minus 25 volts with a five-megasample waveform generator and a 50 megasample logic analyzer, served to a browser over Wi-Fi, targeted at under a hundred dollars retail.
claims.quote_verbatim: we have up to three megahertz analog bandwidth on two channels, plus and minus 25 volts
claims.speaker: Clint Cole
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Clint Cole of Digilent

claims.claim_text: The safe default when a measurement must be taken off an earth reference is to isolate the power supply rather than to lift the earth on the oscilloscope or the laptop; earthing the supply is a deliberate step taken only when the ground system requires it.
claims.quote_verbatim: By default, you want your power supply, whatever that may be, to be isolated.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Support for writing captures to USB mass storage arrived on bench oscilloscopes only around the mid-2000s, because the file-system and USB host stack that a general-purpose operating system supplies for free had to be built from scratch on an embedded platform.
claims.quote_verbatim: that's, that's why the old scopes all struggled even putting stuff on USB drives
claims.speaker: David Kronstein

claims.claim_text: Where a vendor sells bandwidth as a licence key, the hardware can also be modified directly: a top-of-line 100 MHz model was raised in bandwidth by a hardware change rather than by the licence, since the firmware setting ultimately only configures hardware that is already present.
claims.quote_verbatim: they sell a license key option for 100 megahertz bandwidth
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Look at nature and meet nerds

claims.claim_text: Tektronix's 6 series was built on two new in-house ASICs giving 6.25 gigasamples per second per channel with 12-bit resolution, at around twenty-five thousand dollars.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's 6.25 gig samples per second per channel
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The LeCroy HDO8000A preceded the Tektronix 6 series by two months with eight analogue channels at 12 bits and 10 gigasamples per second, plus a separate external trigger and 16 digital channels retained alongside the eight analogue ones.
claims.quote_verbatim: they released the HDO8000A series, which is an eight-channel scope. It's 12-bit as well. It's higher sample rate, 10 gig instead of 6.5 gig.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The analogue input on a logic analyzer such as the Saleae Logic 4 reaches only around six megahertz on a single channel, so it supplements rather than replaces an oscilloscope.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's like six megahertz or something like that. It's, it's, but it's not, it's not bad, but it's not a true scope behavior either. And it's only one channel.
claims.speaker: Akiba

claims.claim_text: Before filtering the noise from a switching regulator module, scope its switching frequency under several loads to establish whether it is fixed or variable, because only a fixed frequency can be targeted with a tuned LC filter, and the module must also tolerate the added output LC.
claims.quote_verbatim: measure its switching frequency under different loads and see if it's a fixed or a variable frequency first
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A control loop can be compensated empirically by injecting a square wave at the input, watching the output on a scope, and adjusting until the response is rounded with no overshoot; this is a valid alternative to analysing the loop mathematically.
claims.quote_verbatim: feed a square wave into your input, not the feedback, feed a square wave into your input, and look at the output on your scope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Probing a modern vehicle's diagnostic port with an oscilloscope shows only the raw digital waveform. CAN bus has been mandated for vehicle communications since about 2009, and its contents cannot be interpreted from the analogue trace without protocol decode; earlier and coexisting physical layers include K-Line, L-Line, LIN and J1850.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you put a, an oscilloscope on that, all you're going to see is, you know, uh, ones and zeros basically
claims.speaker: Collin Kidder
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Earl Sharpe and Collin Kidder

claims.claim_text: Clean edges and correct clock and data assignment confirmed on a scope do not confirm correct protocol behaviour. The scope answers the analogue question, and a logic analyzer with protocol decode answers the framing and content question; using the first when the fault is in the second wastes the debugging effort.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was just using the actual scope just to see the analog signal. Signals look clean.
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The Keysight UXR reaches a true 110 GHz of real-time bandwidth on all channels at 256 gigasamples per second, using an indium phosphide front end rather than an equivalent-time sampling architecture.
claims.quote_verbatim: It is true 110 gig bandwidth
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Real-time bandwidth at that level lets a 50 GHz transmitter be sampled live and its modulation and demodulation analysed inside the instrument, which is the use case that justifies the cost; the customers are largely in high-speed serial links inside FPGAs and similar silicon.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can do the demodulation.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Tektronix was vertically integrated to an unusual degree, manufacturing its own cathode ray tubes and supplying items such as ceramic terminal strips and matched silver solder with the instrument, and the whole stack is visible in equipment from that era.
claims.quote_verbatim: they built CRTs in-house
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Consumer and kit oscilloscopes of the era, including Hickok and Heathkit models, commonly had a free-running rather than triggered sweep, which still made signals visible for the first time but without stable, repeatable presentation of a waveform.
claims.quote_verbatim: It had a free running sweep. It didn't have a triggered sweep.
claims.speaker: Julia Truchsess

claims.claim_text: Electron microscope work requires probing rails at thousands of volts, and an arc-over inside a high-voltage tank destroys scope input channels, so in that field oscilloscopes are treated as consumables; higher-kilovolt tanks are gas filled while SEM tanks are usually oil insulated or potted.
claims.quote_verbatim: I've lost many channels on oscilloscopes to microscopes
claims.speaker: Adam McCombs

claims.claim_text: Some oscilloscopes ship with unpopulated pads for additional memory, so fitting the RAM chips and changing the model configuration converts the unit into the higher model, including features such as the colour screen.
claims.quote_verbatim: This scope has like spare pads for these RAM chips. So you can upgrade them and you can hack the model to be an upgraded model with color screen
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A logic analyzer's timing analysis mode is an oscilloscope with one-bit vertical resolution: it samples asynchronously at a fixed rate such as 50 or 100 megasamples per second and renders the result as square transitions.
claims.quote_verbatim: It works like an oscilloscope. It just samples. At a fixed sample rate.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The Rigol DS1052E entered at eight hundred dollars, dropped to four hundred within a year or two and stayed there for years, later selling around 349 dollars; the floor on a bench scope's price is set by the enclosure, display, probes and silicon rather than by the design.
claims.quote_verbatim: that was $800. Then, then the price went to 400, like a year or two later.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Probes must be compensated against a clean fast edge or every measurement made through them is degraded, and users routinely skip this. Tektronix's John Addis therefore built a very fast, very clean square wave source into the front panel of scopes such as the 485, removing the need for a separate pulse generator.
claims.quote_verbatim: he embedded on the front panel access to a super fast but very, very clean square wave
claims.speaker: Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: Fast oscilloscope front ends are fragile and expensive to repair, so protection circuitry that disconnects the delicate stages on excess voltage or power dissipation, with a panel light indicating it has acted, is a deliberate design feature rather than an accident of later models.
claims.quote_verbatim: he built in all these protection circuits so that it's really, really hard to blow something up in the front end
claims.speaker: Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: The design techniques inside classic HP, Agilent, Keysight and Tektronix instruments were largely never documented in one place; what exists is deliberately scattered across application notes, schematics and patents, because in a specialised market there is no benefit in explaining your methods to competitors.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's spread out very craftily among app notes and schematics and patents so that no one can easily figure out what they did or why
claims.speaker: Tom Lee

claims.claim_text: A digital multimeter's AC accuracy specification typically applies only above about a tenth of full scale, below which its rectifier-based RMS converter becomes nonlinear. Low-level AC measurement therefore needs either a dedicated AC millivoltmeter or an oscilloscope with a preamplifier front end.
claims.quote_verbatim: you need a scope with a pre-amplifier front end
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: There is no known-perfect oscilloscope at the top of the bandwidth range: a published study applying one input to nine of the fastest sampling oscilloscopes in the world produced nine visibly different results, so at those speeds the response of the instrument itself must be understood and taken out of the measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: they rounded up nine of these sampling oscilloscopes, you know, the fastest ones in the world. And they applied the same input to them. Uh, and they all look different.
claims.speaker: Ted Yapo

claims.claim_text: An oscilloscope's bandwidth can be verified on the bench by applying a known fast edge and observing the reproduced rise time, a technique documented in Jim Williams's application notes.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can test the bandwidth of an oscilloscope with a really fast edge
claims.speaker: Ted Yapo

claims.claim_text: Developing fast instrumentation is bootstrapped: verifying a fast front end requires a faster instrument than the one being built, so a project can walk through a 300 MHz scope, a used 1 GHz unit and then a 20 GHz sampling head in under a year. Whoever built the fastest scope at any point in history had no such reference.
claims.quote_verbatim: in order to build, you know, uh, a really fast oscilloscope, I needed a faster one
claims.speaker: Ted Yapo

claims.claim_text: A one-kilohm series resistor into a 50 ohm terminated scope input makes a 20:1 divider whose input impedance is high and broadband, isolating the cable's capacitance and inductance from the circuit under test.
claims.quote_verbatim: 50 Ohm terminate your scope. Uh, and then you have a kilohm resistance so that you have a high impedance that's broadband
claims.speaker: Nash Reilly

claims.claim_text: Triggering exists because acquisition memory is finite: continuous capture at the rate needed to see a microsecond-scale event over days produces unusable volumes of data, so the instrument discards everything not associated with the qualifying event. Oscilloscopes and logic analyzers default to 50 percent pre- and post-trigger capture so the operator sees what happened before the event as well as after.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's what triggering is for. And that's why every scope by default has 50% pre and post triggering
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The useful distinction is bench scope against PC scope, and it is a form factor rather than a capability line: a bench instrument is a self-contained box with its own screen, whether the controls are knobs or a touch interface, while a PC scope has no display or controls of its own.
claims.quote_verbatim: a real scope is one that sits on your bench
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Bench-verifying a high-current switching converter means measuring the dead time between the switch pulses on a scope, because overlap destroys the bridge. The measurement is taken directly on the IGBTs using high-voltage probes with either isolated probes or an isolation transformer on the instrument.
claims.quote_verbatim: you must measure like the dead time between the switch pulses, because if they're on at the same time, they will go boom
claims.speaker: Fredrik Kensander
claims.episode_title: High Current Power Supplies with Fredrik Kensander

claims.claim_text: In a trailing-edge dimmer switching about four amps, the inductance of the supply transformer's secondary produced an 800 volt spike at turn-off that destroyed the internal PCB-mount mains power supply. The spike was narrow but large in amplitude, found by scoping the incoming mains, and the fix is to avoid the transformer or add a few microfarads across its output.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was getting this, like, 800 volt spike
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: An unencrypted bus can be debugged by hanging a scope on it and logging the exchange between the two failing devices. Electric-vehicle CCS charging encrypts its link, so an interoperability failure between one car and one charger cannot be diagnosed that way despite being a physical point-to-point connection.
claims.quote_verbatim: if it was can bus, you could hang a scope on it
claims.speaker: Mike Harrison
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: A traditional bench oscilloscope contains a complete embedded computer because it must both capture and display the data. Headless USB-connected instruments delete that computer and push display and processing onto the host machine, which is already present.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's an embedded computer in there. There's a full computer in there
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: An isolated instrument splits into a control side that talks to the host and a sensor side that performs the measurement, with the barrier crossed by a transformer for power and decoupled signal paths; measurement, auto-ranging and statistics can all run on an FPGA on the isolated side so only summary data crosses.
claims.quote_verbatim: The Jewelscope itself is an isolated design.
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: Bench oscilloscopes are chassis grounded, so their inputs cannot be used to probe a high-voltage or floating node, and even 5 volt or 3.3 volt rails can be damaged if the ground lead lands on them, because the earth path can carry considerable current.
claims.quote_verbatim: Scopes are chassis grounded, folks.

claims.claim_text: A vector network analyzer characterises gain and complex impedance by returning magnitude and phase directly. The same sine waves can be seen on an oscilloscope, but extracting magnitude and phase from them is difficult, which is the practical reason for the separate instrument.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's hard to pick off the magnitude and phase on an oscilloscope
claims.speaker: Joel Dunsmore

claims.claim_text: Connecting an oscilloscope loads the circuit, and a circuit that works only while probed is usually one whose oscillation the probe's impedance is damping. RF test equipment avoids this by defining a common 50 ohm system impedance so the instrument does not perturb the behaviour it measures.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you've ever put an oscilloscope on a circuit and the circuit works when the oscilloscope is connected and you disconnect it and it doesn't work, that's because the impedance loading is maybe stopping that amplifier of yours from oscillating
claims.speaker: Joel Dunsmore

claims.claim_text: The case for owning more than one oscilloscope is concurrent measurement: motor work may need a channel on every winding, and without an eight-channel instrument that means several scopes running together.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're, if you're doing like motor stuff, you might need something on every winding
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: About 10 MHz of bandwidth is enough for a beginner's instrument, and USB scope families including Picoscope, Tektronix and Keysight offer an upgrade path from there without changing the working method.
claims.quote_verbatim: as long as they can do 10 megahertz or so, you know, that's probably enough for people that are getting started
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: When a scope will not decode a serial stream at the rate it is configured for, the assumption to check is the rate itself: measure the bit period on screen and calculate the actual clock rate rather than trusting the configured value.
claims.quote_verbatim: you get desperate enough that you go in there and actually measure the time and calculate the actual clock rate
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: An intermittent fault traced to a lifting bond wire inside a diode, which half-rectified and dropped a rail, was only caught by monitoring every rail continuously on about eight channels across two oscilloscopes; a fault that appears between spot measurements cannot be found by spot measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: I ended up using two scopes. I think I ended up having like eight channels or something, just measuring all the different rails at once
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A modern processor core rail is not a static voltage: it is commanded dynamically between roughly two volts and 0.3 volts and into sleep states as workloads change, and a 15 to 20 watt part can demand 150 amp peaks within ten microseconds of waking, so the scope shows a continuously moving rail rather than a DC level.
claims.quote_verbatim: You look at the core rail and your oscilloscope, it's not going to be sitting there at a nice static one volt.
claims.speaker: Carmen Parisi
claims.episode_title: Switching Converter Engineering with Carmen Parisi

claims.claim_text: Buying a general-purpose scope much beyond two to three hundred megahertz, and certainly beyond 500 MHz, is questionable because the passive probes supplied with it will not reach that bandwidth; a 10:1 passive probe rated to 1 GHz has been made by essentially one manufacturer.
claims.quote_verbatim: the passive probes that come with it won't go that high
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A first oscilloscope should be a model that many other people own, because community knowledge is the only support available when something goes wrong with an unbranded instrument, and the bottom of the market brings noise and instability that a beginner cannot distinguish from circuit faults.
claims.quote_verbatim: one thing that's important for beginners is buying something that other people have
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A dynamic signal analyzer is an FFT instrument working in the frequency domain rather than the time domain like an oscilloscope, and differs from a spectrum analyzer in targeting very low, typically audio, frequencies.
claims.quote_verbatim: unlike a time domain analyzer, like an oscilloscope, it's more of a frequency domain analyzer
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Memory depth and sample rate together fix the capture window: 100 megasamples at one terasample per second is 100 microseconds of record, enough to hold only a handful of packets when a differential probe is bodged onto gigabit Ethernet pairs to catch specific UDP frames.
claims.quote_verbatim: a hundred mega samples at one tera sample per second, which multiplies out to a hundred microseconds of data
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Before digital storage, an oscilloscope had no capture at all; recording a trace meant photographing the screen with a Polaroid camera.
claims.quote_verbatim: You had to take a Polaroid.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The entry price for a real oscilloscope has been roughly stable in nominal terms while the capability behind it has grown enormously: eight hundred dollars bought a dual-channel 20 MHz analogue instrument from a reputable brand in the 1980s.
claims.quote_verbatim: the traditional entry level price was 800 bucks
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The bottom of the market is not a cheaper version of a usable instrument: pocket and toy scopes bottom out around a hundred kilohertz of bandwidth, and even a free or fifty-dollar old analogue scope is generally not worth taking on for that reason.
claims.quote_verbatim: It was like, you know, a hundred kilohertz max
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: A beginner on substandard equipment meets artefacts such as aliasing before having the experience to recognise them as instrument behaviour rather than circuit behaviour, which is the strongest argument against the cheapest scopes for learners.
claims.quote_verbatim: you're going to run into things like anti-alising
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: The modern price ladder runs from a four-channel Rigol or Siglent around four hundred dollars, through an eight-hundred-dollar tier buying a larger touchscreen, higher sample rate and more memory, to four-figure instruments that exceed hobby requirements. The four-hundred-dollar four-channel instrument serves general daily use indefinitely and does not become obsolete.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a kind of a decent jump from 400 to 800 bucks. You get the much bigger screen, touch screen interface
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Bandwidth that will not be used daily should be bought second-hand rather than new; the question to put to a beginner asking about RF capability is what they will actually be doing every day, since RF work at that level is usually done with a pre-certified module.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you want bandwidth, like if you want a one gig bandwidth scope, for example, go to the used market
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The four-channel entry-level scopes sold around four hundred dollars carry hardware capable of 200 MHz and can be unlocked to it, so the licensed bandwidth understates what the instrument on the bench can do.
claims.quote_verbatim: even those four channel entry level 400 buck scopes, they're 200 meg bandwidth, right? You can hack them to 200 meg bandwidth
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Before buying bandwidth to see the analogue behaviour of a fast digital signal, the question to settle is whether a logic analyzer answers the actual question, since most work on a 100 MHz microcontroller concerns bus content rather than edge shape.
claims.quote_verbatim: Are you sure you can't get away with a digital, you know, a logic, a logic analyzer?
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: An oscilloscope's acquisition is inherently discontinuous: it triggers, captures for a window and is blind until it re-arms. Instruments intended for long-duration energy measurement must instead stream without gaps, which also means handling current-range switching without the milliseconds of blind time a multimeter takes to settle its analogue path.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not like an oscilloscope where you have a trigger, you measure for a time, and then you go blank, and then measure again
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty
claims.episode_title: The Joulescope Upgrade with Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: Measuring current by putting a shunt resistor in line and probing it with an oscilloscope runs into the reference problem: neither end of the shunt is at the scope's earth reference. Doing it correctly requires a true differential probe or a differential current probe, which costs more than a dedicated current-measurement instrument.
claims.quote_verbatim: If you don't have a true differential probe, you start talking about a true differential current probe.
claims.speaker: Matt Liberty
claims.episode_title: The Joulescope Upgrade with Matt Liberty

claims.claim_text: Modern oscilloscopes have absorbed several formerly separate instruments: the built-in frequency counter and a good FFT implementation cover measurements, including clock jitter analysis, that once required dedicated boxes.
claims.quote_verbatim: I was able to use an oscilloscope instead and just use like frequency counter function on an oscilloscope
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: The three time-and-frequency instruments differ in what they plot: an oscilloscope shows voltage against time, a spectrum analyzer amplitude against frequency, and a modulation domain analyzer frequency against time, which is what makes the last one able to show the settling behaviour of a frequency source as it loses and regains lock.
claims.quote_verbatim: unlike an oscilloscope, which is voltage versus time
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Where measurements are computed in software rather than in the acquisition hardware, enabling one of them can collapse throughput: on one instrument a single horizontal frequency measurement took the waveform update rate from a million per second to under a thousand, while vertical measurements cost nothing.
claims.quote_verbatim: It drops from four, from a million waveform updates per second to, to under a thousand
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Implementing serial decode, FFT and measurement functions in a custom acquisition ASIC rather than in software means those functions can be enabled without reducing the waveform update rate, which is the practical reason a vendor develops its own silicon.
claims.quote_verbatim: Keysight have the custom ASIC and serial decoding and FFTs and all sorts of stuff is done specifically in the ASIC hardware
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Thunderscope, which grew out of a 2020 hardware contest project, is a four-channel oscilloscope front end presented to a host over Thunderbolt as a PCI Express device rather than over USB.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a four channel PCI scope. So it uses Thunderbolt
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Acquisition silicon in oscilloscopes has a very long service life: one chip carried through a vendor's 1000 and 2000 series and into the TBS basics line, its cheapest scope at around three hundred dollars sold largely into school laboratories, and was still shipping years after introduction.
claims.quote_verbatim: they remarketed it as the TBS, the tech basics series, which was designed to, which is tech's cheapest scope, which is like 300 bucks
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The TM500 modular mainframe supplies power and a chassis into which single-function plug-ins are inserted, including signal generators, multimeters, calibration fixtures, and modules such as a bare op amp with front-panel terminals that can be wired externally into an integrator, differentiator or summer.
claims.quote_verbatim: it allows you to have like a power supply and then you can plug in various modules
claims.speaker: Chris Gammell

claims.claim_text: Serviceability of vintage instruments falls off sharply with date of manufacture: between Tektronix scopes of the 1970s and those of the 1980s the complexity rose steeply with switching power supplies and proprietary custom ICs, and parts that no longer exist make the later ones much harder to repair.
claims.quote_verbatim: just in 10 years the complexity went through the roof you've got like switching power supplies and all this stuff in the newer ones
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Consumer tube oscilloscopes of the 1960s from makers such as RCA, Eico and Heathkit have bandwidths around 100 kilohertz and contain roughly six active devices, so they cannot be used to test anything by modern standards. Their resale value rests on appearance rather than capability, unlike a Tektronix 465 which is worth more because it remains usable.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're the kind of scopes that have like six tubes inside them
claims.speaker: Jeff Keyzer

claims.claim_text: Sigrok began as a logic analyzer project and grew into an open-source layer that talks to multimeters and oscilloscopes for real-time capture across many vendors' hardware. It targets Windows, Linux and macOS and is far too heavy to port onto a low-power microcontroller without stripping it down.
claims.quote_verbatim: they supported multimeters and oscilloscopes. So you can do like real time capture
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The CRT in an analogue oscilloscope deflects its beam electrostatically, using plates rather than the deflection coils used in television and electron-optical instruments, because electrostatic deflection is much faster and more precise.
claims.quote_verbatim: the beam was deflected electrostatically
claims.speaker: Petr Dvorak
claims.episode_title: Freelance PCB Design with Petr Dvorak

claims.claim_text: A leading-edge 14-bit converter at 1 GHz of bandwidth is unlikely to be a single monolithic die, so the acquisition front end is delivered as an all-in-one hybrid module combining several processes in one package.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's an all-in-one scope chip. So it's probably a hybrid chip.
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: The value of a 14-bit acquisition path over a 12-bit one is dynamic range in the spectrum: a signal below fifteen microvolts was recovered from the noise floor on a 14-bit instrument and was not visible on a 12-bit instrument under otherwise identical conditions.
claims.quote_verbatim: I actually pick a 15-microvolt signal out of the noise
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Where bus signals travel in several directions rather than end to end, terminators can be placed mid-bus to absorb the excess energy, and they are tuned empirically by watching the waveform on a scope and minimising overshoot.
claims.quote_verbatim: then you adjusted those with the oscilloscope, minimize the overshoot
claims.speaker: Lee Felsenstein
claims.episode_title: Lee Felsenstein: The Computer Revolution & Counterculture

claims.claim_text: Delayed sweep, also called dual or delayed time base, was the analogue answer to zooming: a second time base runs at a faster sweep speed and starts only after a dialled-in delay from the trigger, so a chosen region far downstream of the trigger event is expanded across the screen.
claims.quote_verbatim: You use your second time base to actually select a faster sweep speed
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Clap on, clap off, lights flicker

claims.claim_text: Analogue storage scopes existed but were priced for well-funded laboratories only, so routine single-shot capture arrived with digital storage; that capability, not the display technology, is what displaced the delayed time base.
claims.quote_verbatim: we had to wait until digital scopes came out before we could single shot capture stuff
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Clap on, clap off, lights flicker

claims.claim_text: A digital oscilloscope has one trigger event and relies on capture memory deep enough to hold the region of interest, which is then zoomed in software. A small number of digital instruments retain two independent time bases with independent triggering to reproduce the analogue delayed-sweep behaviour.
claims.quote_verbatim: a digital oscilloscope, you only have the one, one trigger event, and then you've got to rely on having a big enough capture memory
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Clap on, clap off, lights flicker

claims.claim_text: A JTAG port left enabled gives a usable improvised scope: running boundary scan in bypass mode shifts bits through at up to a few hundred megahertz, sampling pin states without any external instrument.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you run it in like a boundary scan mode, right? And you just do bypass, where it's just shifting bits through
claims.speaker: Colin O'Flynn
claims.episode_title: Small Scale Electronics Manufacturing with Colin O'Flynn

claims.claim_text: A power supply intended for a harsh service life is qualified by deliberately short-circuiting its output with a screwdriver repeatedly while watching the recovery on a scope, then re-running the full acceptance test suite to confirm nothing has degraded.
claims.quote_verbatim: you jam the screwdriver in the output and you put it on the scope a bunch of times and you watch what the recovery looks like
claims.speaker: Todd Bailey

claims.claim_text: Putting a scope across the grounds of two boards while the system is powered demonstrates that no connection is ideal and that the two grounds move relative to each other. Differential signalling absorbs a volt or two of common-mode difference, which is adequate between adjacent boards over a good chassis ground but not over a hundred-foot run.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can usually compensate for a volt or two of common mode noise
claims.speaker: Dave Jones
claims.episode_title: Applied Embedded Electronics with Jerry Twomey

claims.claim_text: Unlocking a 999-dollar four-channel bench oscilloscope yields 800 MHz to 1 GHz of bandwidth with around 500 megapoints of memory plus a dual-channel 100 MHz signal generator, capability that had previously belonged to instruments an order of magnitude more expensive.
claims.quote_verbatim: for $999, you can get a 1 gigahertz or at least 800 megahertz bandwidth four-channel scope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Rigol committed to a multi-year in-house ASIC programme after Siglent took the value position in the low-end oscilloscope market, then priced the result at 999 dollars although the nearest competing instrument was around double that and a 1500-dollar price would still have led the segment on capability per dollar.
claims.quote_verbatim: they started developing these ASICs, like, five years ago
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Test equipment must lead the technology it measures: each new serial data rate requires an oscilloscope fast enough to see it before the first silicon exists, and the instrument maker must also be able to prove that what the instrument displays is correct.
claims.quote_verbatim: the test equipment companies have to have an oscilloscope that's fast enough to look at the signals and they have to have it before, before somebody produces the first silicon
claims.speaker: Martin Rowe
claims.episode_title: The Measurement Blues with Martin Rowe

claims.claim_text: The LMH6518 variable-gain amplifier, containing the differential and variable-gain stages, sits in the front end of almost every modern oscilloscope, and was originally specified to handle 400 millivolts of input offset, which is what supports the front-panel vertical position control.
claims.quote_verbatim: the LMH 6518, which is used in the front end of almost every modern scope
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: A silent redesign of a front-end amplifier reduced its input offset capability below the original 400 millivolts without a part number change, the difference being visible only deep in the datasheet, and scopes built with the later part have been bricked by too much front-end DC offset.
claims.quote_verbatim: they didn't change the part number
claims.speaker: Dave Jones

claims.claim_text: Early wartime radar such as the SCR-270 presented its output on an oscilloscope screen showing range and amplitude only, with interpretation left entirely to the operator's skill.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's a sil scope screen that you'd look at and it would have range and amplitude, nothing else
claims.speaker: Greg Charvat
claims.episode_title: The Terahertz Frontier with Greg Charvat of Teradar

name: Oscilloscope
